sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body: At its core, Tsoro is a simple yet addictive puzzle game that challenges players to drop colored balls into holes on a wooden board. The game is played on a 2x5 grid, with 10 holes evenly distributed across two rows. Before the game starts, players choose a hole to serve as their bank, which earns the most points for each ball dropped into it. The game begins with players picking seven colored balls from the reservoir and dropping them into the holes. Each drop earns points, with the most points awarded for balls dropped into the bank. The goal is to drop as many balls as possible into the bank, while also collecting star balls to unlock unique abilities and special moves. The game's core mechanics are easy to learn, but mastering the strategy and timing required to succeed is a different story. Players must carefully plan their moves, taking into account the colors and positions of the balls on the board to maximize their score. With each level, the game becomes increasingly challenging, as the number of balls to drop and the time limit imposed on players increase. The game's core mechanics are engaging, but it's the addition of star balls that takes Tsoro to the next level. These special balls offer unique abilities, such as changing the color of all balls in a hole or removing a specific color from the board. The star balls add a new layer of strategy to the game, as players must carefully plan their moves to maximize their score and use the star balls effectively. Overall, Tsoro's core gameplay mechanics are simple yet addictive, making it an excellent choice for players of all skill levels.
